earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog MEDs for Mbe' [mtk] are wordlists only (Dieu & Renaud 1983 ALCAM; Jacquot & Richardson 1956); no grammar or phonology exists.

sources.citation: WALS Online, language Mbe' (wals code mbz), datapoints table
sources.note: No stress or prosodic feature coded; the only datapoint is 142A Para-Linguistic Usages of Clicks (value 'Affective meanings').

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog, 'OLAC resources in and about the Mbe' language' (ISO 639-3 mtk), Wayback snapshot 2026-03-11
sources.note: Nothing; only aggregator records (Glottolog, PHOIBLE, WALS, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List). No SIL or other archive holds any primary resource for mtk.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2016. Ethnologue 19th ed., entry 'Mbo'' [mtk] (Wayback copy)
sources.note: Nothing. Records: 1,490 speakers (2000); North West region, Donga-Mantung division, north of Magba town on the regional boundary, and West region, Noun division; dialects Mbaw, Mbe'; Unwritten; 'People are shifting to Tikar [tik] outside of the home. Distinct from Mbe [mfo] of Nigeria, which is in the Ekoid group.'

sources.citation: Watters, John R. 2003. Grassfields Bantu. In Nurse & Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, 225-256. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Nothing about Mbe' stress. p. 231 lists '(e) Mbi' (a:Mbaw, Mbo)... no estimate. Refers to area known as Mbɔ Plain, on northern border of Yamba. Each of thirteen villages has its own language, some more closely related to Tikar. Same as Mbe' in Grimes (2000:44) (Ginny Bradley pc).' Section 2.4 Tones (p. 227) is a general statement that Grassfields Bantu languages are tonal (H/L, floating tones); it names other languages, never Mbe'.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, language mbee1250, inventory 'Mbe (GM 1599)', source page 1599_mtk
sources.note: Nothing on stress (segment inventory with two tone bars ˦ ˨). The cited source is 'Pohlig, James. 1981. The Mbe verb: A description of the verb system of Mbe, a language of Northern Cross River State, Nigeria (unpublished)' — i.e. the Ekoid Mbe [mfo] of Nigeria, not this Cameroonian language; the PHOIBLE assignment to mbee1250 is a misidentification.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page + md.ini for mbee1250 (Hammarström et al.); Glottolog 5.1 CLDF sources.bib (local copy) grepped for [mtk]
sources.note: Nothing. MEDs are wordlist_or_less (Dieu & Renaud 1983 p.48; Jacquot & Richardson 1956, 2 pp.); n_desc_refs = 0. The full hh bibliography tags exactly five works with [mtk]: Dieu & Renaud 1983, Binam Bikoi et al. 2012, Jacquot & Richardson 1956, McCulloch 1954 (ethnographic), Watters 2003 (overview) — no grammar, sketch, phonology or dictionary.
Nothing; one-line stub citing only Ethnologue.
